t:
(a) Notwithstanding any other provision of this Act, except as provided in subsection (b), and 30 days after the date on which the President determines whether to declare a major disaster because of an event and any appeal is completed, the Administrator shall publish on the Web site of the Federal Emergency Management Agency a report regarding that decision that shall summarize damage assessment information used to determine whether to declare a major disaster. 
    (b) The Administrator may redact from a report under subsection (a) any data that the Administrator determines would compromise national security. 
    (c) In this section—
        (1) the term “Administrator” means the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency; and 
        (2) the term “major disaster” has the meaning given that term in section 102 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 5122).

fable.w: The tempting reading is that publishing a report on a public website, and the mention of an "appeal", amounts to public participation. But the report is published only after the President's decision and any appeal are complete, so it is one-way disclosure and not consultation with outside parties before a federal decision. The reference to an appeal only sets the timing of the report; the section does not itself grant any outside party a right to appeal or sue.
fable.s: the Administrator shall publish on the Web site of the Federal Emergency Management Agency a report regarding that decision that shall summarize damage assessment information used to determine whether to declare a major disaster

qwen_block.w: This section requires the publication of a report summarizing damage assessment information after a decision has been made. It does not require consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before the decision is made. The mention of 'any appeal is completed' refers to the procedural timeline for publication, not a grant of participation rights or a right to sue that influences the decision-making process itself. Therefore, it is a transparency/reporting requirement, not participation.
qwen_block.s: the Administrator shall publish on the Web site of the Federal Emergency Management Agency a report regarding that decision that shall summarize damage assessment information used to determine whether to declare a major disaster.

opus.w: The section only requires FEMA to publish a summary of damage assessment information after the disaster decision and any appeal are finished. This is disclosure after the fact, not input from outsiders before a federal decision. The reference to 'any appeal' just sets the timing; this section doesn't create or grant any right to appeal or sue.
opus.s: 30 days after the date on which the President determines whether to declare a major disaster because of an event and any appeal is completed, the Administrator shall publish on the Web site of the Federal Emergency Management Agency a report regarding that decision
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes," for two reasons. The section mentions "any appeal," which could suggest an outside party (such as a State) challenging the decision. It also requires a public report on FEMA's website. Neither counts as participation. The appeal is only mentioned as a timing trigger; this section doesn't grant anyone a right to appeal. And the report is published after the decision has already been made. It is one-way transparency, with no consultation, comment period or input from outsiders before the decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the publication of a report summarizing information used in a decision that has already been made. It does not require consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before the decision is made. Transparency via publication is distinct from participation in the decision-making process as defined.
qwen_chat.s: the Administrator shall publish on the Web site of the Federal Emergency Management Agency a report regarding that decision that shall summarize damage assessment information used to determine whether to declare a major disaster.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that publishing a report on a website constitutes "participation" because it makes information available to the public. However, the definition explicitly states that participation involves consulting or coordinating with people *before* making a decision, or granting rights to sue/object. Mere publication of a report after a decision has been made is transparency, not participation in the decision-making process. There is no requirement for public comment, hearing, or consultation with outside entities regarding the disaster declaration itself.
